picks.rationale: The Cubs are a strong home favorite at 71-51, while the Cardinals are 61-60. Chicago has won eight of its last 10 games, demonstrating excellent recent form. The Cubs' starting pitcher, Clay Holmes, despite a recent fibula fracture, has a 2.86 ERA, which is significantly better than the Cardinals' starter Matthew Liberatore's 5.15 ERA. Public betting money has consistently backed Chicago, with support ranging from the high 80s to mid 90s in percentage across multiple line checks. This pick leverages the Cubs' superior pitching matchup and strong home record against a Cardinals team with a struggling starter, offering good value at plus money.

Cincinnati's probable pitcher, Chase Burns, owns a stronger season line with a 2.61 ERA and 1.12 WHIP, compared to Miami's Sandy Alcantara's 3.52 ERA and 1.18 WHIP. The total has fallen to 7.5, indicating a pitching-dominant game, which favors the Reds' stronger starter. While Miami has a slightly better record, the Reds are playing at home where they can arrange their better relievers around a narrow lead. The Reds moneyline at -112 offers fair value, especially considering the pitching advantage and home-field advantage.

Boston's starter, Jake Bennett, boasts a 3.17 ERA and 1.04 WHIP, a substantial advantage over Pittsburgh's Bubba Chandler's 1.38 WHIP. The Red Sox have a positive road moneyline record and have performed well away from home. Despite public money leaning towards Pittsburgh, the line movement has seen Boston's moneyline price improve from the mid -140s to -120, indicating sharp money on the Red Sox. This favorable pitching matchup and value in the line movement make the Red Sox a strong play on the moneyline.

The Tampa Bay Rays are in excellent form, with a 74-46 overall record and an impressive 41-18 at home, winning nine of their last ten games. While Orioles starter Kyle Bradish has a better ERA (3.69) than Rays starter Steven Matz (5.48), Matz is unlikely to have a long leash, and the Rays' offense has been hot, scoring 30 runs in their last three games. The Rays have a strong run-line record of 70-49 overall, and their overall team strength and recent offensive surge at home make them a confident pick to win by multiple runs.

Braves pitcher Chris Sale is active and has been in dominant form, with 151 strikeouts in 123 innings this season, averaging 7.19 strikeouts per start. He has recorded at least eight strikeouts in each of his last three starts, including 11, nine, and eight punchouts. Sale's 30.4% strikeout rate and 15.4% swinging-strike rate further support his ability to hit the over on this prop. The Diamondbacks' contact-heavy offense creates some resistance, but Sale's recent performance and underlying metrics indicate he can achieve seven or more strikeouts within a normal six-inning outing.
